digest.top_line: BEACON-HCC: new North American allocation framework puts SBRT and TARE first-line for solitary HCC, 96.6% vs 72.4% expert concordance vs BCLC 2025.
digest.tldr: Hepatobiliary carries the day, and it is an RT-relevant framework rather than a trial: BEACON-HCC moves EBRT/SBRT out of BCLC's post-TACE-failure slot into first-line for solitary disease (Class 1A/1B/1C) and keeps a role at Class 1D. Consensus only, no prospective outcome validation.

sites.intro: One consensus framework, no new outcome data: the question for rad onc is whether first-line SBRT survives validation against BCLC's TACE-first sequencing.

studies.name: BEACON-HCC
studies.tldr: New North American HCC allocation framework; 96.6% expert concordance vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025, with SBRT/TARE elevated to first-line.
details: 🔍 Modified Delphi, 20 North American multidisciplinary experts (incl. rad onc); voting June 2025, >20% disagreement triggered revision + repeat vote
📊 External validation: 18 independent experts, 29 real-world cases, blinded to the framework
📊 Concordance 28/29 (96.6%) with BEACON vs 21/29 (72.4%) with BCLC 2025
🔍 EBRT/SBRT and TARE are first-line options for solitary HCC (Class 1A/1B/1C), not BCLC's second-line-after-TACE-failure slot

details.text: 🔍 Where BEACON re-slots RT vs BCLC 2025
subdetails: Class 1A/1B/2: stages aligned with BCLC, but framework elevates SBRT and TARE
Class 1D (Vp1-2, satellite, or infiltrative margin): potential role for TARE, SBRT, and resection despite BCLC advanced (C)
Class 3A: staging aligned, framework elevates SBRT and TARE
Class 4A (>50% burden): EBRT/TARE not routinely indicated outside palliation

details: 📐 Rad onc dissent is on record: for Class 1A one respondent held SBRT should be *preferred*, not just useful
🔗 RT evidence cited: NRG/RTOG 1112 (63% Vp3/4) trend to better OS with SBRT vs sorafenib, p=0.06; TACE+EBRT RCT beat sorafenib in locally advanced disease
🔗 DOSISPHERE personalized dosimetry cited for TARE: ORR 71 vs 36%, OS 26.6 vs 10.7 mo
⚠️ Consensus, not outcomes: no prospective validation, and the panel concedes expert consensus is not a surrogate for improved clinical outcomes
⚠️ Concordance is measured against expert opinion, and the framework's own authors seeded the case set (29 cases, panel-submitted)
⚠️ Class-level agreement was not uniform: Class 3A cleared only 11/16 (68.8%) initially before revision

verdict.rationale: Delphi consensus document, not a trial. Codifies practice already common in North America; pilot concordance measured against expert opinion, not outcomes. No prospective validation.
verdict.audience: HCC across stages, North American practice patterns

studies.significance: The operative change for a rad onc is slot position: SBRT and EBRT move from BCLC's post-TACE-failure fallback to a first-line option for solitary HCC (Class 1A-1C) and stay on the table for Vp1-2 invasion (Class 1D), where BCLC assigns systemic therapy. That reframes the tumor-board argument for referring an ablative-candidate lesion to RT rather than defending it after TACE fails.
studies.monday_clinic: For a solitary liver-confined HCC in a non-surgical candidate, this framework supports offering SBRT or TARE up front rather than only after TACE failure; it does not support locoregional therapy for >50% tumor burden (Class 4A), where systemic therapy remains the stated mainstay.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Modified **Delphi consensus**, 20 North American experts spanning hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology. Four teleconferences plus email, with voting in June 2025; any statement drawing **>20% disagreement** was revised and re-voted.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: The pilot metric was **concordance**: the most-selected treatment among clinicians vs the framework's recommendation across 29 panel-submitted cases. External validators (n=18) worked **without access** to the BEACON framework.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **EBRT/SBRT and TARE are elevated to first-line** for solitary HCC (Classes 1A, 1B, 1C) on the basis of higher CR probability and longer TTP vs TACE, and remain options for **Vp1/Vp2 invasion** (Class 1D). They are **not routinely indicated** for Class 4A (>50% tumor burden) outside palliation. No dose or fractionation is specified anywhere in the framework.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Concordance **28/29 (96.6%)** with BEACON vs **21/29 (72.4%)** with BCLC 2025. The BCLC discordances clustered on vascular invasion: experts chose systemic plus locoregional therapy in four Vp cases where BCLC recommends systemic alone.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: BCLC 2025 confines TARE and EBRT to second line when TACE is not possible. BEACON cites **NRG/RTOG 1112** (SBRT vs sorafenib, **p=0.06** for OS, 63% Vp3/4) and **DOSISPHERE** (**ORR 71 vs 36%**, **OS 26.6 vs 10.7 mo** with personalized dosimetry) as the basis for moving radiation-based therapy forward.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HCC managed in North American multidisciplinary centers with access to transplant, TARE, and SBRT. Does not represent globally derived practice settings, nor patients with Child-Pugh C disease or ECOG PS ≥2, for whom symptom-directed care is stated.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Concordance against **expert opinion is not an outcome**, and the 29 cases were submitted by panel members themselves, inviting case-selection and confirmation bias. Agreement was also uneven by class: **Class 3A cleared only 11/16 (68.8%)** on first vote.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SBRT and EBRT move from BCLC's post-TACE-failure fallback to a first-line option for solitary HCC (Class 1A-1C), and stay eligible for Vp1-2 invasion (Class 1D) where BCLC assigns systemic therapy. No dose or fractionation is specified, so the framework wins the referral argument but leaves technique to the reader.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Adjuvant therapy after CR is explicitly not recommended, and ICI plus locoregional combinations stay case-by-case rather than routine. Systemic therapy is preferred for Class 3B (Vp3/4) and for Class 4A, where >50% tumor burden is reframed as systemic disease rather than an intermediate-stage TACE candidate.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Resection is preferred without CSPH, transplant with it, and the framework keeps surgery on the table beyond early stage after response to locoregional or systemic therapy. Class 1D (Vp1-2, satellite) is explicitly resectable in selected patients despite BCLC calling it advanced, with 5-yr RFS 10-25% cited.

open_questions: Prospective outcome validation of BEACON vs BCLC allocation
TARE with personalized dosimetry vs ICI systemic therapy in Vp1-2 disease
Sequencing of locoregional and systemic therapy for downstaging

papers.title: BEACON-HCC: Best evidence and north american consensus on treatment allocation for hepatocellular carcinoma
authors: on behalf of HCC-Live Steering Committee
papers.abstract: Background : Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Optimal treatment decisions are challenging, and existing treatment allocation frameworks may not fully reflect the evolving therapeutic landscape or contemporary clinical practices in North America. Methods : Using a modified Delphi process, a multidisciplinary panel of 20 North American experts in hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology developed a consensus-based treatment framework for HCC, termed the BEACON-HCC system. The framework was informed by current evidence and expert opinion through iterative discussion and voting. In a pilot study using 29 real-world patient cases, we assessed concordance between external expert recommendations and BEACON-HCC recommendations and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) 2025 treatment recommendations. Results : The BEACON-HCC treatment allocation framework diverges from prior frameworks by incorporating nuanced clinical features such as degree of intrahepatic tumor burden and vascular invasion, and adverse tumor prognostic markers, to align treatment allocation with tumor biology and therapeutic potential. Key innovations include the incorporation of emerging modalities such as external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), transarterial radioembolization (TARE), and systemic-locoregional combination therapies. In the pilot exercise, expert treatment decisions showed 96.6% concordance with BEACON-HCC recommendations and 72.4% concordance with BCLC recommendations. Conclusions : BEACON-HCC is a consensus-based framework for treatment allocation that incorporates the expanding range of therapeutic options available to patients in the North American HCC population. Expert treatment decisions showed a high concordance with the BEACON-HCC system; further validation using empiric clinical data is planned through the HCC-Live Consortium.
